findings.title: Passing datetime via Celery kwargs may break inbound assignee sync
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which includes `queued` as a `datetime.datetime` object. This dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`. With Celery's default JSON serializer (or Sentry's JSON-based task serialization), a raw datetime object cannot be serialized, causing an `EncodeError` at dispatch time. This breaks every inbound assignee sync that carries an `assignment_source` (the new code path), so the fix itself will fail in production.

findings.title: Unconditionally passing `assignment_source` keyword may break existing integrations
findings.body: The task now unconditionally passes `assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`, even when `parsed_assignment_source` is `None`. Existing concrete integration implementations that follow the old task interface and do not accept an `**kwargs` or an explicit `assignment_source` keyword will raise `TypeError`, breaking outbound assignee sync for all flows that don't provide a source (e.g., manual assignments). The task should only pass this keyword when it is non-None, or all implementations must be updated to accept it.

findings.title: `queued` default evaluated at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated at module import time, not at instantiation. All `AssignmentSource` instances created without an explicit `queued` share the same timestamp (the import time), which is usually incorrect for audit/logging purposes. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.
